title: POC to PROD: Hard Lessons from 200+ Enterprise GenAI Deployments - Randall Hunt, Caylent

domains.rationale: The entire talk is about transitioning enterprise GenAI from POC to production across 200+ deployments spanning Fortune 500 to startups, covering organizational, technical, and economic dimensions.

summary:
Randall Hunt, CTO of Caylent—an AWS Premier Tier Consulting Partner—presents practical lessons from 200+ enterprise GenAI deployments, focusing on the transition from proof-of-concept to production. The talk covers the AWS infrastructure stack including Bedrock, SageMaker, and Trainium/Inferentia custom silicon (~60% price-performance improvement over Nvidia GPUs). Hunt demonstrates multimodal video search using pooled frame embeddings with Titan V2, a sports footage processing pipeline with ffmpeg-based highlight detection, and video annotation techniques using SAM 2. Caylent's three main engagement types are self-service productivity tools, business function automation, and product monetization.

Key lessons include: eval and embeddings alone are insufficient—understanding access patterns is critical; speed matters but UX matters more, as generative UI can mitigate inference latency; prompt engineering has proven "unreasonably effective" versus fine-tuning as models improved, with Claude 3.7 to 4 showing zero regressions while 3.5 to 3.7 did show regressions; context management—finding minimum viable context and optimizing it over time by removing irrelevant information—is a key differentiator; and knowing your economics is essential to avoid bankrupting the company.

Customer examples illustrate knowing your end user: CloudZero's generative UI with cached React components for AWS cost visualization; remote-area workers receiving PDF page screenshots instead of 200MB downloads; and hospital nurses who rejected voice bots due to noisy environments, preferring chat interfaces. Hunt strongly advises against doing math in LLMs and highlights cost optimization through prompt caching, batch processing (50% off on Bedrock), and tool usage. The talk closes with an emphasis on finding minimum viable context for correct inference and continuously optimizing it, requiring deep knowledge of end users and their workflows.
whyItMatters: These concepts form a cohesive framework for moving enterprise GenAI from proof-of-concept to production. The software engineering concepts (vector store selection, batch inference, prompt caching, generative UI, evaluation pipelines, context optimization) represent the implementation toolkit, while the AI concepts (multimodal embeddings, prompt engineering vs fine-tuning, context management, human-centered design, inference economics) provide the strategic decision-making framework. Together they address the full lifecycle: infrastructure selection (Trainium/Inferentia, Bedrock, vector stores), system design (context management, faceted search, generative UI), quality assurance (evaluation methodology, regression testing), cost management (batch inference, prompt caching, avoiding LLMs for math), and user experience (knowing your end user, UX over raw speed). The unifying thread is Hunt's emphasis that system inputs, outputs, and access patterns are fundamental while specific models and tools are incidental and will evolve—so engineers should invest in evaluation, context optimization, and cost awareness rather than over-fitting to any particular model or framework.
temporalContext: The talk was published on YouTube on July 23, 2025, and was delivered on the AWS Partner Network's AI LIVE! stream at re:Invent 2025. The companion Caylent blog post (Part 2) was published January 16, 2026, providing written confirmation of all major claims. Key quantitative claims were current as of mid-2025: AWS Bedrock batch inference at 50% off was confirmed by AWS documentation in June-August 2025; the ~60% Trainium/Inferentia price-performance improvement is attributed to Caylent's deployment experience rather than an independent AWS benchmark. The Claude model upgrade observations (3.5 to 3.7 showing regressions, 3.7 to 4 showing zero regressions) reflect model versions available as of the talk date. BrainBox AI was acquired by Trane Technologies, adding organizational evolution context. The AWS Bedrock pricing, model availability, and custom silicon landscape may have evolved between the talk date and the research date of August 2026.
takeaways: GenAI is not a magical pill; what CTOs read in the Wall Street Journal is not necessarily the latest technology
Evaluation processes are the critical layer proving system robustness beyond vibe checks; vibe checks evolve into eval sets
System inputs and outputs are fundamental; choice of LLMs and tools is incidental and will evolve over time
Eval and embeddings alone are insufficient—understanding access patterns and user behavior leads to much better results
Prompt engineering has proven unreasonably effective as models improve; Claude 3.7 to 4 showed zero regressions
Speed matters but UX matters more—fancy UI can mitigate inference latency; if slower and more expensive, you will not be used
Context management is a key differentiator: finding minimum viable context and optimizing it over time by removing irrelevant information enables better inferences
Know your end user: hospital nurses preferred chat over voice bots in noisy environments; remote users needed lightweight PDF delivery
Don't do math in an LLM—it is the most expensive possible way of doing math
Know your economics: prompt caching, tool usage, and batch processing (50% off on Bedrock) are essential cost optimizations

concepts.name: Multimodal Embeddings
concepts.explanation: Amazon Titan V2 embeddings that combine text and image modalities, enabling text-to-video search through pooled frame-level embeddings stored in vector databases.
concepts.importance: Foundational to the multimodal video search demonstrations in the talk. Represents the shift from text-only retrieval to multimodal understanding in production GenAI systems.

concepts.name: Prompt Engineering vs Fine-tuning
concepts.explanation: Prompt engineering has proven 'unreasonably effective' compared to fine-tuning as models improve, reducing the need for fine-tuning. Hunt observed this across hundreds of deployments.
concepts.importance: Challenges the assumption that fine-tuning is necessary for production quality. As models improve, prompt engineering alone may suffice, reducing cost and complexity.

concepts.name: Context Management as Differentiator
concepts.explanation: Injecting user context (browsing history, current page) and optimizing context windows enables more strategic inferences. Hunt identifies context management as a key competitive differentiator for GenAI applications.
concepts.importance: Shifts focus from model selection to context engineering. The ability to construct optimal context is what separates production-grade systems from demos.

concepts.name: Minimum Viable Context
concepts.explanation: The concept of finding the smallest amount of context needed for correct model inference, then continuously optimizing by removing irrelevant information so the model has less to reason over.
concepts.importance: A closing emphasis of the talk—this principle simultaneously improves accuracy, reduces latency, and lowers cost, making it a holistic optimization target.

concepts.name: AI Agents and Tool Orchestration
concepts.explanation: Multi-agent architectures for enterprise applications. Hunt notes that tools and LLMs are incidental to the system and will evolve, while inputs, outputs, and access patterns are fundamental. Trivial tool definitions like get_current_date are unnecessary when you control the prompt.
concepts.importance: Provides a framework for thinking about agent architecture: focus on system specifications (inputs, outputs) rather than specific tool or model choices that will change over time.

concepts.name: LLM Inference Economics
concepts.explanation: Understanding the cost structure of LLM inference including token costs, batch processing discounts (50% on Bedrock), prompt caching discounts, and the cost implications of different deployment options including custom silicon.
concepts.importance: Hunt warns that without understanding economics, GenAI deployments can bankrupt a company. Cost literacy is presented as an essential engineering skill for production GenAI.

concepts.name: Model Evaluation Methodology
concepts.explanation: Anthropic's approach where vibe checks become the first evals, evolving into simple boolean metrics and structured eval sets. Evaluation is the critical layer proving system robustness beyond intuition.
concepts.importance: Provides a practical starting point for teams without formal eval infrastructure—begin with vibe checks and systematically evolve them into automated metrics.

concepts.name: AWS Custom AI Silicon (Trainium/Inferentia)
concepts.explanation: Purpose-built AI accelerator chips offering approximately 60% price-performance improvement over Nvidia GPUs, with tradeoffs including less HP RAM than H200 GPUs and the requirement to use the Neuron SDK.
concepts.importance: Represents a significant infrastructure cost optimization option for training and inference workloads, with practical tradeoffs that engineers must evaluate for their specific use cases.

concepts.name: Human-Centered AI Design
concepts.explanation: The principle that knowing your end user and their operating environment is critical for AI system success. Hospital nurses rejected voice bots in noisy environments; remote-area users needed lightweight PDF delivery instead of 200MB downloads.
concepts.importance: Demonstrates that technical sophistication is irrelevant if the deployment context doesn't match user needs. User environment constraints must drive interface and delivery choices.

concepts.name: GenAI Is Not a Universal Solution
concepts.explanation: Hunt dispels the myth that GenAI is a magical pill, noting that what CTOs read in the Wall Street Journal is not necessarily the latest technology. System inputs and outputs are fundamental while LLMs and tools are incidental and will evolve.
concepts.importance: Sets realistic expectations for GenAI deployment. Prevents over-investment in hype-driven use cases and encourages focus on fundamentals: access patterns, evaluation, and user needs.

concepts.name: Intelligent Document Processing
concepts.explanation: Using AI for document understanding that achieves faster and better results than human annotators, as part of business function automation engagement type.
concepts.importance: Represents one of Caylent's three main GenAI engagement types and demonstrates practical ROI beyond chatbots for enterprise document-heavy workflows.

concepts.name: Vector Store Selection
concepts.explanation: Choosing between PostgreSQL, Redis/MemoryDB, and OpenSearch for vector storage based on cost, latency, and access pattern requirements. PostgreSQL is preferred for disk-based HNSW indexes; Redis/MemoryDB is extremely fast but expensive due to RAM requirements; OpenSearch supports HNSW on disk.
concepts.importance: Selecting the wrong vector store leads to either excessive cost or insufficient performance. Hunt explicitly states eval and embeddings alone are insufficient and understanding access patterns is critical to making this decision.

concepts.name: Batch Inference
concepts.explanation: Running inference requests asynchronously at a 50% cost reduction on AWS Bedrock, suitable for non-real-time workloads that process large datasets.
concepts.importance: A core cost optimization strategy that can halve inference costs for asynchronous workloads. Hunt emphasizes knowing your economics to avoid bankrupting the company.

concepts.name: Prompt Caching
concepts.explanation: Caching prompt prefixes to reduce inference costs, with Bedrock offering reduced pricing on cache reads. Prompt placement in the prompt structure affects caching effectiveness.
concepts.importance: Enables significant cost reduction for repeated prompt patterns and is part of the economics toolkit Hunt recommends for production GenAI systems.

concepts.name: Generative UI
concepts.explanation: Dynamically crafting and caching UI components (React) from LLM output to mitigate inference latency and provide evolving, personalized tool experiences.
concepts.importance: Directly addresses the principle that speed matters but UX matters more—generative UI can mask multi-second inference latency through perceived responsiveness, driving user adoption.

concepts.name: Evaluation Pipeline Design
concepts.explanation: Building evaluation processes that evolve from informal vibe checks to structured boolean metrics and eval sets, following Anthropic's methodology where vibe checks become the first evals.
concepts.importance: Evaluation is explicitly called out as the critical layer proving system robustness. Without evals, teams cannot detect regressions across model upgrades or measure quality improvements.

concepts.name: Model Regression Testing
concepts.explanation: Tracking performance across model upgrades to identify regressions. Hunt observed regressions from Claude 3.5 to 3.7 but zero regressions from 3.7 to 4, demonstrating the importance of maintaining eval sets across upgrades.
concepts.importance: As models evolve, regression testing ensures production quality is maintained. Without it, silent degradation can occur when switching model versions.

concepts.name: Context Window Optimization
concepts.explanation: Finding the minimum viable context needed for correct inference and iteratively removing irrelevant information so the model has less to reason over, improving both accuracy and cost.
concepts.importance: Identified as a key competitive differentiator. Optimizing context directly impacts inference quality, latency, and cost simultaneously.

concepts.name: Faceted Search Architecture
concepts.explanation: Multi-dimensional filtering that goes beyond vector similarity search. Hunt emphasizes that embeddings alone cannot handle faceted search and filters, requiring complementary retrieval mechanisms.
concepts.importance: A common pitfall in RAG systems—relying solely on vector similarity without faceted filtering leads to poor results for queries requiring structured filtering.

concepts.name: Multimodal Video Search Pipeline
concepts.explanation: Processing video by sampling frames, generating pooled frame embeddings with Titan V2, and storing in vector databases (Elasticsearch) for text-to-video semantic search. Includes ffmpeg-based audio extraction and event detection.
concepts.importance: Demonstrates a production-grade architecture for multimodal search that goes beyond text-only RAG, applicable to media indexing and content discovery use cases.

concepts.name: Cost-Driven System Architecture
concepts.explanation: Designing GenAI systems with explicit cost awareness: avoiding LLMs for mathematical computation, leveraging batch inference and prompt caching, and understanding per-request unit economics.
concepts.importance: Hunt warns that without understanding economics, GenAI deployments can bankrupt a company. Cost must be a first-class architectural concern, not an afterthought.

concepts.name: Video Annotation for Model Performance
concepts.explanation: Technique of annotating video frames (e.g., marking court lines on static camera angles) to improve model question-answering performance, using tools like SAM 2 for segmentation.
concepts.importance: Shows that visual context augmentation can significantly improve multimodal model performance without model changes, a practical optimization technique.

sections.title: GenAI Application Categories and Business Moats
sections.summary: Three engagement types: self-service productivity tools, business function automation with intelligent document processing, and monetization. Discussion of building moats through inputs and outputs, with emphasis on evaluation as the critical layer.

sections.title: AWS Infrastructure and Model Stack
sections.summary: Details of AWS infrastructure including Bedrock and SageMaker, Trainium and Inferentia custom silicon with ~60% price-performance improvement over Nvidia GPUs, model selection from Claude to Llama, vector store options (PostgreSQL preferred, Redis/MemoryDB fast but RAM-expensive, OpenSearch with HNSW on disk), and context management as a key application differentiator.

sections.title: Key Lessons: Eval, Speed, and Prompt Engineering
sections.summary: Core lessons including eval and embeddings not being sufficient, faceted search needs beyond embeddings, speed matters but UX matters more, avoiding trivial tool definitions like get_current_date, prompt placement for effective caching, prompt engineering proving unreasonably effective versus fine-tuning, Claude 3.7 to 4 showing zero regressions, and knowing your economics to avoid bankruptcy.

sections.title: Evaluation Methodology and Generative UI
sections.summary: Anthropic's eval methodology where vibe checks become first evals evolving into boolean metrics. Cloud Zero customer example using generative UI with dynamically crafted and cached React components for AWS infrastructure cost visualization, enabling personalized and evolving tool experiences.

sections.title: Knowing Your End User and Economics
sections.summary: Customer examples illustrating end-user knowledge: remote-area workers receiving PDF page screenshots instead of 200MB downloads, hospital nurses rejecting voice bots for chat in noisy environments. Advice against doing math in LLMs, and cost optimization through prompt caching, tool usage, and batch processing at 50% off on Bedrock.

sections.title: Closing: Minimum Viable Context and Invitation
sections.summary: Hunt closes by emphasizing the importance of finding the minimum viable context needed for correct inference and continuously optimizing that context over time by removing irrelevant information so the model has less to reason over. This requires deep knowledge of end users and their workflows. He invites attendees to reach out with compelling use cases, noting Caylent has talented engineers ready to build for customers.

organization.name: Caylent
organization.summary: Caylent is a cloud services company and AWS Premier Tier Services Partner that helps organizations build, run, and evolve intelligent systems on AWS. Founded in 2015 and headquartered in Irvine, California, Caylent has 501-1,000 employees and serves customers from startups to Fortune 500 enterprises. The company holds the AWS GenAI Industry Solution Partner of the Year award (2024) and won GenAI, Migration, and Security Consulting Partner of the Year in 2025. Caylent is also an Anthropic Preferred Services Partner, AWS Managed Services Provider, and achieved the AWS Agentic AI Specialization. The talk presents lessons from 200+ enterprise GenAI deployments by Caylent, covering AWS infrastructure (Bedrock, SageMaker, Trainium, Inferentia), evaluation methodology, context management, and cost optimization.
organization.status: Active and growing. 2025 Inc. 5000 honoree (#352). Won 10 AWS Partner of the Year Awards including GenAI, Migration, and Security Consulting Partner of the Year in 2025. Achieved AWS Agentic AI Specialization. Continues to deliver GenAI deployments at scale with hundreds of concurrent customers.

technologies.label: Amazon Bedrock Managed Foundation Model Platform
technologies.summary: Amazon Bedrock is the central managed foundation model platform discussed throughout the talk. Hunt describes it as the primary service for deploying GenAI in production, with specific emphasis on batch inference (50% cost reduction verified by AWS pricing page and engineering blog), prompt caching (75% off cache reads), and model selection spanning Claude, Llama, and Amazon models. The talk also references Bedrock AgentCore for agentic AI workloads, as used in the CloudZero Advisor deployment with five specialized agents. Hunt frames the choice between Bedrock and SageMaker as a managed-convenience vs custom-control tradeoff.
technologies.role: Primary infrastructure platform for enterprise GenAI deployment; enables batch inference, prompt caching, multi-model selection, and agentic AI orchestration

technologies.label: AWS Custom AI Silicon (Trainium/Inferentia)
technologies.summary: AWS Trainium and Inferentia are purpose-built AI accelerator chips discussed as offering approximately 60% price-performance improvement over Nvidia GPUs. Hunt notes practical tradeoffs including less HP RAM than H200 GPUs and the requirement to use the Neuron SDK. The ~60% figure is attributed to Caylent's deployment experience and corroborated by the companion blog post (January 2026). These chips represent a major infrastructure cost optimization lever in the talk, directly supporting Hunt's emphasis on knowing your economics.
technologies.role: Infrastructure cost optimization option for training and inference workloads; alternative to Nvidia GPU-based deployments with ~60% price-performance improvement

technologies.label: Vector Search & Retrieval Infrastructure
technologies.summary: Vector store selection is a critical infrastructure decision in the talk, with Hunt preferring PostgreSQL for its balance of HNSW index support on disk and cost-effectiveness. Redis/MemoryDB is noted as extremely fast but expensive due to RAM requirements. OpenSearch also supports HNSW on disk. The talk emphasizes that embeddings alone cannot handle faceted search and filters, requiring complementary retrieval mechanisms. Elasticsearch is used in the Nature Footage demo for storing pooled frame embeddings. The companion Caylent blog post confirms PostgreSQL preference and Redis/MemoryDB cost tradeoff.
technologies.role: Infrastructure selection decision demonstrating the importance of understanding access patterns; also serves as the storage layer for multimodal search demos

technologies.label: Multimodal Embeddings & Video Search Pipeline
technologies.summary: The multimodal embeddings and video search pipeline combines Titan V2 multimodal embeddings, Nova Pro for frame understanding, pooled frame embedding techniques, ffmpeg for video processing, and SAM 2 for annotation. The Nature Footage demo shows text-to-video search using pooled frame samples stored in Elasticsearch. The sports footage pipeline includes audio transcription, embedding generation, event detection with push notifications, and an ffmpeg-based amplitude spectrograph hack for highlight detection. Video annotation (marking court lines on static camera angles) demonstrably improves model QA performance. The companion Caylent blog post confirms this architecture.
technologies.role: Primary technical demonstration showing end-to-end multimodal video search architecture; illustrates how embeddings, multimodal models, and video processing tools combine in production GenAI systems

challengeSeeds: Given a multimodal video archive of 10,000 clips, build a semantic search system using pooled frame embeddings. Compare HNSW vs IVF flat index performance and cost. Add faceted filtering and measure where embeddings alone fall short.
Design an evaluation pipeline that starts with vibe checks for a customer support chatbot and evolves into automated boolean eval sets. Track regressions when upgrading from Claude 3.5 to 3.7 to 4.
Optimize a Bedrock-based inference workload to reduce monthly costs by 50% using batch inference, prompt caching, and tool placement strategies without degrading output quality.
Build a context optimization loop that iteratively removes information from a RAG context window while measuring answer accuracy. Find the minimum viable context for 95% correct responses.
Create a generative UI component that dynamically renders and caches React components from LLM output, achieving sub-2-second perceived latency despite multi-second inference times.
Given a hospital nurse workflow in a noisy environment, evaluate why a voice bot fails and design a chat-based alternative. Measure transcription accuracy degradation at different noise levels.
